I farm this small plot of beans here in the North West, and I have been doing it for many years. The land is mine, so I take care of it well, but cash is always tight — beans do not need much fertilizer like maize does, and they put something back in the soil themselves, so I do not waste my little money on NPK for this plot. I will put some of the manure from my goats and a bit of household waste, and I keep my own seeds from last year's harvest like my neighbors do. I intercrop with a little sorghum or millet as usual, and me and my wife and son will do most of the work ourselves, though at weeding time I may call two or three young men from the village to help for a few days.
